source.title: Beyond Linear Concepts: Discovering and Aligning Non-Linear Concept Manifolds in Large Language Models
source.authors: Tido Specht; Elias Krey; Nils Neukirch; Nils Strodthoff

record.tranche_reason: The study compares independently discovered representations across model scales, model families, and training stages using concept-based alignment (CBA), a different alignment measure from the original sources.
record.gate_note: Included results that measure alignment across models or compare alignment metrics. Excluded within-model layer alignment, concept composition, and multilingual English–Mandarin results: they do not measure the claim versions about cross-model scaling, paired cross-modal alignment, or recurring features. R1's numeric metric comparison concerns adjacent-layer correspondence, not cross-model convergence.
record.test_reason: Result 5 compares CBA alignment within one family (Qwen3 4B/8B/32B, same recipe) with a cross-family pair at matched scale (Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct vs Qwen3-8B). Within-family alignment is strong and cross-family alignment is weak, which bears on V7. The authors also frame Result 4 as an empirical counterpoint to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis. No scale series across independent families is run, so V1's scaling trend is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also note that the cross-family pair keeps a weak diagonal and middle-layer block, suggesting corresponding functional blocks across families. They present training-dependent English–Mandarin concept sharing as a counterpoint to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
record.recipe_differences: Uses UMAP/HDBSCAN-discovered fuzzy concept manifolds and CBA rather than the original sources' methods; it compares model and layer concept geometry rather than testing the original cross-domain similarity claim directly.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported adjacent-layer structures depend on the alignment metric: linear CKA obscures details that PCA-512 and NLMCD/CBA reveal, while CBA has the highest Neighbor z. No systematic sweep over input distributions or neighbour counts is reported.

fits_no_version.finding: Within-model adjacent-layer alignment structure depends on the metric. Linear CKA saturates and hides blocks that PCA-512 and CBA reveal; CBA has the highest Neighbor z (2.515 vs 1.287 for linear CKA).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within-model layer-similarity structure depends on the similarity metric chosen.

fits_no_version.finding: Post-training stages of Llama-3.1-8B keep CBA above 0.8. The largest shift is base to SFT, and DPO–RLVR stays near 0.85–0.86.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Finetuning only moderately alters a pretrained model's concept geometry.

fits_no_version.finding: English–Mandarin shared concept mass above a shuffled control is about zero in GPT-2 (0.0009), 0.024 in Llama and 0.039–0.049 in Qwen3. The authors call this a counterpoint to the Platonic Representation Hypothesis.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-lingual concept sharing within a model depends on training rather than being universal.

record.problems: The study does not measure model capabilities or test a monotonic increase in alignment with size. Cross-model CBA values are shown as figures without numerical scores. The model suite is limited to models up to about 32B parameters, and the authors note that discovered concepts depend on the extraction corpus.

untested.parts: No series of independently trained, different-family models across scale or capability. The only cross-family comparison is one 8B pair, and the scale comparisons are within the Qwen family only.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer.
No test of whether specific features recur across models; concept matching is done only across finetuning stages of one model.
Metric dependence is shown only within a model, across layers. Cross-model alignment is computed with CBA alone, with no variation of metric, neighbour count or inputs.
Shared data and training recipe are not manipulated independently of family, and no plateau with scale is examined.

missing.what: Numeric CBA values for the cross-model matrices (only described qualitatively in the text)

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 'challenges' label is dropped. One matched-scale cross-family pair, with figure-only values, cannot test a scaling trend, and the Qwen scale pairs are same-recipe, not independent. The V6 links rested on a within-model method benchmark, which the gate note itself excluded. The R6 rows are same-initialization drift, not convergence. The cross-family tokens were aligned by character-span pooling over 1,024 observations.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not measure model capability or test whether alignment rises monotonically with size or performance.
No vision–language model comparison or image–caption paired-data alignment.
No comparison across random initialization seeds.
CBA compares concept geometry; the study does not test mapping, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired observations.
It does not test whether the same interpretable features or circuits recur across models.
The study compares alignment metrics but does not vary neighbour count or systematically test out-of-distribution inputs.
Shared training data and objectives are not independently manipulated, so their causal contribution is not established.

relationships.condition: Qwen3 within-family pairs (4B–8B, 8B–32B) vs the cross-family Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct–Qwen3-8B pair
relationships.reason: Within-family (shared recipe) alignment is strong while cross-family alignment is substantially lower, with only a weak diagonal (r5-qwen-4b-8b, r5-qwen-8b-32b, r5-llama-qwen). This fits alignment being far from complete and tied to shared training; the evidence is figure-only, with no numbers.
relationships.display_finding: Qwen3 pairs sharing a training recipe aligned strongly, while the Llama–Qwen3 pair showed substantially lower alignment with only a weak diagonal.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: challenges
reader_labels.reason: The different-family, matched-scale comparison has substantially lower CBA than within-family Qwen comparisons, qualifying the broad cross-architecture convergence claim (r5-llama-qwen).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Neighbor z differs across alignment methods, with CBA highest; the paper also states that the choice of metric changes which structures are visible (r1-pca-z, r1-cka-linear-z, r1-cka-rbf-z, r1-cba-z).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Adjacent-layer NN Alignment Score across the four methods
reader_labels.reason: All methods give nearly perfect adjacent-layer scores, so metric dependence is less evident for this measure than for Neighbor z (r1-pca-nn, r1-cka-linear-nn, r1-cka-rbf-nn, r1-cba-nn).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: Alignment remains above 0.8 across stages, with DPO and final RLVR particularly close, indicating substantial but incomplete preservation of concepts (r6-all-pairs-above-08, r6-dpo-rlvr).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: Cross-family comparison and comparisons involving SFT
reader_labels.reason: Cross-family alignment is substantially lower, and comparisons involving SFT have lower intermediate alignment than the closely aligned DPO–RLVR stages (r5-llama-qwen, r6-sft-comparisons).
